# SK9012 — `skala.jsonc` tries to pin a canonical version

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

`skala.jsonc` has a `canonical.version` property. The version lives in the `# skala:canonical begin` marker in `.editorconfig`, beside the bytes it names, and nowhere else. Delete the key; `skala config check` fails on it without `--strict`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Tool |
| Default severity | error |
| Scope | Compilation |
| Needs a compilation | no |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 0.6 |

## Why

A version recorded away from the thing it versions is a version that drifts: the marker's `version=` and `sha256=` travel together with the payload they describe, and a second copy in another file is a second thing to keep in sync with nothing checking that it is. The only key under `canonical` is `drift`.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
{ "canonical": { "version": "0.1.0", "drift": "error" } }
```

Write:

```csharp
{ "canonical": { "drift": "error" } }
```

## When it does not fire

The value is not inspected — `"version": null` fires the same as a real number. The check does not short-circuit, so an invalid `canonical.drift` in the same object is reported alongside it as `SK9008`. ⚠ The id once carried a second meaning, an I/O failure written as a bare literal in the formatter; that use was renumbered to `SK9015`, and `ToolDiagnosticIds_AreNeverBareLiterals` exists so it cannot recur. An old report naming `SK9012` against a `.cs` file was the I/O failure.
